startup.name: GBrain
startup.one_liner: A personal or team assistant that works while you sleep
startup.description: GBrain is a cloud hosted AI assistant, like ChatGPT or Claude, that runs in the background, remembers everything given to it and ships with preloaded skills. A user hands it a job at night and reads the result in the morning, alone or as a team. Pricing is likely a subscription. Team of 3 in San Francisco, Spring 2026 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: Test assumes the company was accepted, so this is only a note. Prior about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent third party range). Up for a technical team and strong product feel, down for a crowded general assistant category with direct frontier lab competition and no narrow wedge in the description.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because a general cloud assistant that does overnight tasks is exactly what the model labs ship themselves: there is no named customer group, no clear edge over a lab product and many similar agent applicants each batch, so reviewers ask why this team wins.

Same space companies like Tasker AI and Khoj had little funding found, and Niles died, while the labs ship memory and background agents themselves.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C needs a durable product or a platform position in AI assistants. The category could be commoditised by model vendors and operating systems, and by that time acquisition by a larger software company is more likely than another private round, which is why so few companies in the cohort reach this stage.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the product is overtaken by assistant features from the model labs and stalls, or the team is acqui hired. Niles died, Clara Labs sold after raising an A, and Tasker AI and Khoj stayed small. A larger outcome requires finding a workflow where overnight agents with memory clearly beat a lab product.

killers.risk: Model labs and big platforms ship the same background agent with memory
killers.evidence: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google add memory, scheduled tasks and agent modes to their assistants, with large user bases.
killers.mitigation: Pick a narrow audience such as a team workflow and integrate deeply with their tools.

killers.risk: No clear wedge so growth and retention are weak
killers.evidence: The description is general and a general assistant competes on brand and price against free tiers.
killers.mitigation: Find one job type users return for daily and price on outcomes.

killers.risk: Trust and security for team data slow adoption and add cost
killers.evidence: Teams that store documents and credentials in a third party agent need audits and access controls.
killers.mitigation: Offer private deployment and clear data controls early.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a cloud agent with memory, a task queue and skills on top of frontier models is feasible for a small team in three months. The hard parts are reliable long running execution, safe handling of credentials and keeping quality as models change.

takeover_risk.rationale: The labs already offer memory and scheduled agent features and have the distribution, so they can match any general assistant in months. The startup also depends on their models, so a pricing or policy change hits it directly.

evidence.claim: Millions of people already pay for assistant subscriptions, so the category has demand.
Workflow automation tools like Zapier and funded agent startups show teams pay to offload routine work.

roadmap.goal: Pick a narrow high value use case
actions: Interview 20 heavy assistant users about overnight jobs
Ship a prototype used daily by 20 people

roadmap.goal: Raise above $500K within 12 months of the batch
actions: Reach paying subscribers or team accounts
roadmap.proof: Revenue run rate and a lead investor
Net revenue retention above 100 percent and $1M recurring revenue

pros.point: Large and proven demand for AI assistants
pros.evidence: Hundreds of millions of people use assistants and many pay for them.

pros.point: Technically feasible for a small team
pros.evidence: The product can be built on frontier models, so the team can ship quickly and iterate on usage.

brand.name: GBrain
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "GBrain" --era 2022+: invented or proper noun, 6 characters, 1 word
weaknesses: Generic brain naming is common in AI
brand.rationale: Short names did well in older YC eras but the 2022+ data shows no clear effect. The name hints at memory, yet many AI tools use brain names, so it will not differentiate from lab products like ChatGPT or Claude.

narrative.headline: A well timed assistant idea in the most crowded category, where the model labs are the real competitors.
narrative.general_summary: GBrain offers a cloud assistant with memory and skills that works overnight. Demand for assistants is proven, and a small team can build it fast, so a seed is plausible if usage is strong. The core problem is that frontier labs ship the same features with huge distribution, so the company needs a narrow wedge. Analogs such as Tasker AI, Khoj and Niles stayed small or died while Clara Labs raised an A and sold. Estimates are slightly below the B2B cohort anchors, and uncertainty is wide because the product is general.

assumptions: Only the input file was used for the company; market sections use general knowledge and homepage URLs.
